EXPERIENCE

Atlas Ridge Software, Boston MA
Senior Frontend Engineer
Lead frontend for the analytics product, a React and Next.js application used by about
11,000 weekly users.
Rebuilt the charting layer on top of visx after Highcharts licensing became a problem,
which cut the vendor cost line and reduced the charts bundle from 420KB to 96KB.
Took Largest Contentful Paint on the dashboard from 4.2s to 1.3s by moving to server

regressions before release in two years.

zero, and ran the two rounds of screen reader testing with actual users that followed.
Mentor three engineers and run the frontend guild's fortnightly session.

jd_text:
Senior Frontend Engineer, Design Systems
Remote (US, Eastern or Central) | Design Engineering | $165,000 - $195,000

We are a 400 person company with eleven product teams, and right now each of them has a
slightly different button. The design systems team exists to end that. We are four people,
two engineers and two designers, and we are hiring our third engineer.

This is a platform role. Your users are other engineers and designers. Nothing you ship
will have your name on it in the product, and the measure of your success is that other
teams stop writing the component you gave them.

What you will do
- Build and maintain the component library: React, TypeScript, headless primitives on top
  of Radix, published as a versioned package
- Own the design token pipeline. Tokens are authored in Figma and need to arrive correctly
  in CSS, in the React package and in our React Native app without three people maintaining
  three copies
- Make accessibility a property of the system rather than a thing each team remembers.
  Keyboard interaction, focus management, ARIA semantics, screen reader behaviour
- Write and maintain the documentation site. A component nobody can find does not exist
- Work in a monorepo with Turborepo, and care about the build and release tooling
- Run adoption: talk to product teams, migrate them, and take their complaints seriously

Requirements
- 5+ years of frontend engineering with deep React and TypeScript
- Component API design. You can explain why a prop should be a slot instead of a boolean
- Serious CSS: cascade layers, custom properties, container queries, and the confidence to
  write it without a utility framework
- Accessibility at a practical level. WCAG 2.2 AA, and experience testing with NVDA or
  VoiceOver rather than just running an automated scanner
- Storybook, and visual regression testing that the team kept using
- Monorepo tooling: pnpm or yarn workspaces, Turborepo or Nx, and package versioning
- Experience maintaining a library that other teams consumed, including the migration and
  deprecation work that comes with it

Nice to have
- Design tokens with Style Dictionary or Tokens Studio
- React Native, or any cross-platform system work
- Figma plugin development
- Web Components, or an interest in framework-agnostic distribution
- Animation work beyond transitions: Framer Motion, or the Web Animations API
- A public design system, library or documentation site we can look at

Our process is a portfolio conversation, a component API design exercise, an accessibility
and CSS deep dive, and a collaboration round with one of our designers.
